entries.name: GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN
entries.description: The refresh token from connecting the mailbox with the gmail.metadata scope. Google doesn't rotate it, so this value keeps working until the owner revokes access, changes their password, leaves it unused for six months, or (for an External consent screen still in Testing) seven days pass. The instance keeps a sealed copy in its database in case Google ever returns a new one; replacing it here (after reconnecting) takes over.
howToGet: Have the mailbox owner connect the mailbox to the instance's OAuth client with access_type=offline, prompt=consent and exactly the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata, for example through Google's OAuth 2.0 Playground using the client's own credentials (add https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground as an authorized redirect URI).
The connector stops if the token holds any other Gmail scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.labels, gmail.send, gmail.compose or https://mail.google.com/), so don't add them.
Copy the refresh token straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: GMAIL_USER
entries.description: Which mailbox to read: me (the account that connected, the default) or that account's address. One mailbox per instance. Not a secret, but it names the mailbox.
howToGet: Leave empty for me. Each further mailbox needs its own instance.

entries.name: GMAIL_LABEL_NAMES
entries.description: Whether user label names are kept: keep (the default) keeps names such as Bridal or Vendors, leaving out any with an @ or four digits in a row; drop keeps label ids only, for a mailbox whose labels are named after customers.
howToGet: Leave empty for keep. Use drop if labels in the mailbox carry customers' names.
